steps: 2 is greater than 1, so the $2 note is worth more.

steps: Count up from 60¢ to 100¢: that is 40¢.

items.q: A ruler costs $4. A book costs $5. You pay with a $10 note. How many dollars is your change?
items.hint: Find the cost of both things first.
steps: 4 and 5 make 9, so the two things cost $9.
Count up from $9 to $10: that is 1 dollar.

slips.say: 9 is how much the two things cost. The change is what the shop gives back.
That is 10 minus 4 only. Add the book as well.

tpl.q: A ruler costs ${a}. A book costs ${b}. You pay with a $10 note. How many dollars is your change?
tpl.hint: Find the cost of both things first.
steps: {a} and {b} make {s}, so the two things cost ${s}.
Count up from ${s} to $10: that is {t} dollars.

items.q: Make 50¢ with one 20¢ coin and some 10¢ coins. How many 10¢ coins do you need?
items.hint: One 20¢ coin leaves 30¢ to make with ten-cent coins.
steps: 50 minus 20 is 30, which is three 10¢ coins.

slips.say: One 20¢ coin and two 10¢ coins make only 40¢. Count up to 50¢.
Five 10¢ coins make 50¢ on their own. This way there is a 20¢ coin too.

items.q: What is the fewest number of notes and coins that make $73? Use $1, $2, $5, $10 and $50.
items.hint: Take the biggest piece that fits first.

slips.say: Try a bigger piece first. A $50 note covers most of $73.

tpl.q: What is the fewest number of notes and coins that make ${n}? Use $1, $2, $5, $10 and $50.
tpl.hint: Take the biggest piece that fits first.
steps: Take the biggest piece that fits, then the next biggest, until nothing is left.

items.q: Mei has a $5 note, a $2 note and a $1 coin. She uses one, two or all three pieces. How many different amounts can she make?
items.hint: List the amounts with one piece, then two pieces, then all three.

slips.say: 3 is only the amounts with one piece. Try two pieces together, and all three.
8 is the most money she can make. How many different amounts are there?

items.q: Make a shop puzzle for a grown-up. Choose a price and a note. Ask how much change. Check the answer with your play money.
items.hint: Pick the price first, then the note.
steps: Choose a price and a note that is worth more.
Count up from the price to the note with your play money.
Ask a grown-up, then check together.
